question: Does the GTK2 GtkIconView rubberband use the KDE Selection role from the active palette and preserve the resulting item selection after release?

runtime.widget: Native GtkIconView in GtkScrolledWindow; MULTIPLE mode; 8 folder rows; four columns
runtime.input: X11 drag from empty view space across all eight items; capture while held, release, capture again

behavior: selection-box-color is optional; when unset, the widget uses style->base[GTK_STATE_SELECTED]
the rectangle fill uses that color with alpha; its outline uses the same color opaque

translation.gtk2_rc_behavior: R201 maps IconView base[SELECTED] to the active KDE Selection face; this RC leaves selection-box-color unset, so GTK2 falls back to base[SELECTED].

result: The GTK2 rubberband fill follows the active KDE Selection face through the existing base[SELECTED] mapping in four actual GTK2 palette previews. Pixel samples outside the rectangle remain at the current View face; samples inside agree with the 64/255 blend within one 8-bit RGB level. All eight cells remain selected after release.
limits: This is private GTK2 runtime evidence, not a live SR10.4 comparison or human visual approval.
The source and runtime evidence establish the GTK2 mechanism; they do not establish that VUE XmpIcon uses the same alpha, rectangle geometry, outline or post-release appearance.
The GTK2 selected-cell fill still covers full item rectangles, while the paired VUE selection in R200 covers label text only.
Other GTK2 widgets, focus/hover comparisons and full visual acceptance remain open.
